posts.text: A deep dive on Oriana Power Ltd - Full article The company has grown its profits 244X in 5 years. The revenues have grown 59X in 5 years to reach ₹1813 Cr. The order book stands at ~₹7,000 Cr. ROE is 40%. On paper it is looks incredible right but the more you read, the more questions you get. The economic reality of the company hidden thanks to Accounting Standard 21 is now brought forward.

posts.text: I am sorry that can’t be right. Here real capex costs incurred by real Greenfield green Ammonia projects in India ACME Gopalpur , 0.4 MTPA: ₹20,000 crore, so about ₹5 lakh or $5,700 per tpa. (July2026) ACME Paradeep , 0.8 MTPA: ₹34,000 crore, so about ₹4.25 lakh or $4,800 per tpa.(July2026) ACME Tamil Nadu (2022 ): ₹52,474 crore for 5 GW solar, a 1.5 GW electrolyser and 1.1 Mt of ammonia, so about $5,400 per tpa. Electrolyser alone costs $900-1300/MT and for a 60000 MTPA plant you would need 300MWp (solar+wind) . A generous 3cr/MWp would mean 900cr on RenW alone

posts.author: justinwilson
posts.community: Oriana Power - SME play on Renewable Energy
posts.text: Oriana is one company that foresee disruptions and act accordingly. However, they are moving from a high ROE (high margin / high asset turnover) business to low ROE business. Revenue share expectation FY 27 = 60% Solar & 40% BESS FY 28 = 30% Solar & 60-70% BESS, some Green hydrogen FY 29 = 30% Solar & 40% BESS, 30% Green hydrogen First thing to ask Gemini is how this will impact the bottom line. My prediction is that bottom line will grow at only half the rate of top-line revenue growth.

posts.text: First of all how will they recognise sale of a SPV as revenue? They can only recognise profit/loss on the sale and ideally it should be in other incomes but they will mostly recognise it in op revenues. Revenues are already recognised as EPC sales to SPVs in previous FYs. SPV sale is purely monetization of “book profits” and not additional revenue.
